data.headline: ‘One Can See Similarities to 1973,’ Exxon Mobil Economist Says of Iran Oil Shock
data.summary: The chief economist of Exxon Mobil, which is dependent on the Middle East for much of its oil-and-gas production, said the energy market shock from the ongoing war with Iran is structurally similar to the Arab oil embargo in 1973.  “When I look back on past recessions..., I think one can see similarities to 1973 in the sense that you’re talking about physical barrels, physical cubic feet that aren’t flowing,” Tyler Goodspeed said during a discussion at the Economic Club of New York on Tuesday.  Goodspeed, who led the White House Council of Economic Advisers in President Trump's first administration, said that global output has become less energy and oil intensive since the 1970s, and many economies learned from the twin shocks of that decade by building strategic petroleum reserves.
